rationale: fp-convert is a tiny, FP-arithmetic-dominated SingleSource benchmark with no source metadata available, so the profile gives little to discriminate on; the strategy is broad but moderate-strength obfuscation. SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because a conversion benchmark is arithmetic-dense, making expression substitution maximally effective and cheap, and its weights keep cost/risk penalties low so it fires widely. FLA and BCF are the main structural deterrents and are kept strong, but their moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights prevent over-application in a program whose small hot kernels would otherwise suffer disproportionate slowdown. SPLIT is enabled weakly (high security weight withheld) since a tiny function count limits its benefit, serving mainly as a low-risk enabler for FLA. IBR and ICALL carry elevated CorrectnessRisk weights because FP-heavy code with calling-convention-sensitive conversions and possible FP exceptions makes indirect dispatch the likeliest correctness hazard, so they apply selectively; IGV is kept at moderate weights as a cheap global-state indirection that adds diversity without threatening FP semantics. Overall the table biases toward arithmetic and control-flow transformation while gating the dispatch-level passes behind cost and correctness penalties to preserve benchmark validity.
